This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation, assailing the judgment and award dated 25.10.2021 in MVC No.745/2016, on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT-II at Aland, Kalaburagi district (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal').

3. Having taken note of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties and also taking into account the injuries sustained by the claimant as per Ex.P3 - wound certificate and the disability certificate at Ex.P9, I am of the view that, the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability to the extent of 15%.

Taking into consideration that, the accident is of the year 2015 and as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, monthly income of the claimant would be Rs.8,000/- and by applying the appropriate multiplier of 16, the claimant is entitled for Rs.2,30,400/- (Rs.8,000x12x16x15%) towards loss of future earning capacity.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1052 HC-KAR 4.

Taking into consideration the grievous injuries sustained by the claimant as per the wound certificate and the disability certificate marked before the Tribunal, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:
 Heads Amount Pain and suffering Rs.60,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up Rs.24,000/- period (Rs.8,000x3) Loss of amenities Rs.60,000/-
Loss of future of earnings Rs.2,30,400/- Towards food and nourishment and Rs.40,000/- attendant charges

Medical expenses Rs.1,25,237/- Future medical expenses Rs.20,000/-
Total Rs.5,59,637/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.4,40,837/-
Enhancement Rs.1,18,800/-
Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,18,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:1052 HC-KAR 5.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed in part.
II. The appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,18,800/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
